GraceRequirements.Annotation: Userland operating environment for the Internet built from capability-provided plugins above a generic Rust kernel.
GraceRequirements.Keywords: Rust, plugin runtime, capabilities, browser, agents, UI composition, workspaces, activity memory

Goals.Goal: Preserve what the user was doing, why they were doing it, and what resulted instead of storing only pages and URLs.
Provide browser, agent, UI, memory, search, and integration behavior through replaceable plugins.
Keep one runnable end-to-end proving slice from the earliest kernel build through each roadmap milestone.

Users.User: People doing long-running research, development, purchasing, writing, and monitoring work on the Internet.
Plugin authors integrating browser engines, models, UI surfaces, storage, search, and external tools.

Constraints.Constraint: Nothing above the kernel receives hidden privilege or product-specific special treatment.
Capability authority is default-deny and auditable.
RPC and event transport retain separate semantics, failure behavior, and authority.
Event sourcing is never the automatic storage model for every domain.
External side effects require visible intent and explicit confirmation at the policy boundary.
